sections.h2: How do I sell a house fast in Belton, Missouri?
sections.html:
Belton sellers can list the house, sell it themselves or take a cash offer, and the right choice usually depends on the house's condition and whether it has tenants. Because Belton runs a rental registration and inspection program and Cass County handles taxes and recording, a fast sale goes smoothest when those pieces are lined up in advance.

A rental house is the case that surprises people most. Since January 1, 2025, every rental unit inside city limits has to be registered with Belton, and the city inspects between tenants. An owner selling a tenant-occupied house, or a buyer planning to rent it out, should read that program before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: Where is Belton, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Belton is a city in northwestern Cass County that belongs to the Kansas City metro area. It sits four miles from the Kansas border on Missouri Route 58, west of I-49 and U.S. 71. Raymore is four miles east, Peculiar is seven miles southeast and Grandview, in Jackson County, is five miles north. The city covers 14.25 square miles of land at about 1,099 feet in elevation.

Belton was platted in 1871 and probably took its name from surveyor Capt. Marcus Lindsey Belt, and its post office has run since 1872. Growth came after World War II. The census counted 1,233 residents in 1950, 4,897 in 1960 and 12,270 in 1970, and the 2020 count was 23,953. The Census Bureau estimates 26,193 for July 1, 2025. In 2020 the median age was 36.1, 33.7 percent of 9,171 households had children under 18 and 7.7 percent of the 9,936 housing units were vacant.

Most of the city is in Belton School District #124, which runs six elementary schools, two middle schools and Belton High School. A portion of eastern Belton is in the Raymore-Peculiar School District. Metropolitan Community College taxes the Belton district, and a branch of the Cass County Public Library is in town.

sections.h2: What do Belton homes and rents look like?
sections.html:
Belton is closer to an even split between owners and renters than most suburbs, which explains the city's rental program. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates show 59 percent of homes owner-occupied and a median owner-occupied value of $203,200.

sections.h2: What are Belton's rental registration and code enforcement rules?
sections.html:
All rental units inside Belton must be registered, and inspections happen between tenants, after one leaves and before the next moves in. The program took effect on January 1, 2025, under an ordinance the council approved on October 10, 2023.

  • Registration costs $20 per unit and renews every 12 months.
  • A $50 late fee applies to each 30-day period a registration is past due.
  • An inspection done after the tenant has already moved in costs $20.
  • Reinspection fees begin after two failed inspections and are $20 each.

Email rental@belton.org to schedule an inspection or ask questions. Separately, the Neighborhood Improvement and Code Enforcement division, part of Community Development, enforces the property maintenance and use ordinances. Since October 28, 2024 all active violations appear on the city's eTRAKiT portal, where a free public account lets you see them, apply for permits and schedule inspections. Check the portal for open violations on your address before you accept an offer, since a buyer's title search or lender may find them.

sections.h2: Can I run a short-term rental in Belton?
sections.html:
Only with city approval, and the rules are narrow. The council adopted Ordinance 2025-4950 on November 25, 2025, and under it every short-term rental needs a registration and a special use permit. The staff report describes the registration fee as $70 a year, an inspection fee of $50 and a $150 permit fee, a minimum of $270 to start.

The ordinance caps occupancy at two adults per bedroom plus one more adult per dwelling, up to ten guests including children. Owners pay the city's 5 percent hotel and motel tax monthly, and an owner may register no more than five units. The staff report described locations limited to the Old Town Belton area and parcels over three acres, so ask Community Development which location rule covers your address.

A temporary exception tied to the 2026 FIFA World Cup allowed registrations only from June 1 to July 31, 2026, and it expired on August 1, 2026. Operating outside the permitted rules can bring fines from $200 to $500, and each day may count as a separate offense. Buyers who plan to use a Belton house as a rental should confirm what the city allows before they close.

sections.h2: How do Cass County taxes work when I sell in Belton?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due on receipt of the bill and no later than December 31, with the U.S. postmark deciding timeliness. The Cass County Collector mails bills in November, and penalties and fees can reach 25 percent in the first year of delinquency. Residential property is assessed at 19 percent of market value, and the tax is the assessed value divided by 100 times the levy rate.

Cass County's guide for buyers and sellers says the new owner is responsible for paying the whole bill by December 31, that taxes are generally prorated between the parties at closing and that no money is paid to the Collector at the time of sale. Taxes are a lien that stays with the property, so a buyer becomes liable for anything unpaid. Property can be sold at the annual tax certificate sale on the fourth Monday in August at the Harrisonville courthouse when taxes remain unpaid.

If you sell during the year and a bill arrives in your name, tell the Collector the new owner's name and address. The Collector is Chris Molendorp at 2725 Cantrell Road in Harrisonville, 816-380-8377, and the Assessor's office is at 2733 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8400.

sections.h2: Where is the deed recorded after a Belton sale?
sections.html:
The deed is filed with the Cass County Recorder of Deeds at 102 E. Wall Street in Harrisonville, open from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays, phone 816-380-8118. The Recorder does not prepare documents, so use a title company or a real estate attorney.

Cass County also runs a fraud alert system at casscounty.com/fraud, which notifies you when a document is recorded under your name. A deed that is not recorded is valid only between the parties and anyone with actual notice under RSMo 442.400, which is why closing agents file immediately. For a Belton owner who needs to move quickly because of repairs, tenants, an inherited house or back taxes, a cash purchase can shorten the schedule while the same inspection, tax and recording steps apply.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house before selling it in Belton?
faqs.a: Rental units inside Belton city limits must be registered, at $20 per unit per year. Inspections are required between tenants, so a vacated rental should be inspected before the next occupant or buyer moves in.

faqs.q: Can I list my Belton house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only with registration and a special use permit under Ordinance 2025-4950. The minimum startup cost in the staff report is $270, and owners pay the 5 percent hotel and motel tax.

faqs.q: When are Cass County property taxes due for a Belton house?
faqs.a: On receipt of the bill and no later than December 31. A late payment can add penalties and fees as high as 25 percent in the first year of delinquency.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax at a Belton closing?
faqs.a: Cass County says taxes are generally prorated between buyer and seller, and no money goes to the Collector at the sale. The new owner pays the full bill by December 31.

faqs.q: How many people live in Belton?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 23,953, and the Census Bureau estimates 26,193 on July 1, 2025. Belton sits in northwestern Cass County within the Kansas City metro area.
